rationale:
Decision: split into four children. All four reuse comparator-accepted declarations, with identical lean_name and byte-identical frozen lean_statement. The split creates no new proof work, and this node's own Lean becomes a compiled 15-line assembly.

1. Why split.
- A leaf may append exactly one declaration under its own name, with no helper declarations and no imports (leaf_verification.check_source_delta).
- Unsplit, this node would need one monolithic proof of about 130 lines. That proof would cover the Carathéodory strip estimate, Lebesgue's inequality via the Stieltjes measure, the left-slope limit and Fatou.
- Lebesgue's inequality needs the Stieltjes route: MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc and MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv are unknown constants after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission` (rechecked).
- The selected proof factors along its own steps into four reusable obligations:
  - strip_distribution (steps 2-3): a monotone F that controls the strip masses of an arbitrary G, by Carathéodory splitting along the open strip.
  - lintegral_deriv (step 8): Lebesgue's inequality ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(F′) ≤ ofReal(F(b) − F(a)) for monotone F.
  - left_slope (the limit part of step 4): left difference quotients in [0, ∞] at a point of differentiability.
  - monotone_majorant (steps 4-7 and 9): g := L·liminf_j ofReal(F_j′) is measurable and dominates liminf_j Z_j a.e., and Fatou gives the integral bound. It depends on lintegral_deriv and left_slope.
- Step 1 (b ≤ a) needs no separate case, because every child holds for arbitrary a, b.

2. Reuse.
- The twin node cbr_slice_mass_majorant (root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.convergence_tools-a1.slice_majorant-a1) has this node's byte-identical frozen type. It is accepted (candidate c68b3d1c).

- The parent's own decomposition (decomposition-v1 of convergence_tools) already planned to reuse the twin's cbr_smm_* grandchildren for this node.
- The twin's four children are accepted, with candidate commits, and are the children proposed here:

- Each name occurs on exactly one DAG node, so _existing_lean_name_problem allows the reuse (accepted checkpoint, identical type).
- _solve_children maps each key to the existing node id, so no new nodes or handoffs are created. The proposed edge monotone_majorant → {lintegral_deriv, left_slope} resolves to exactly the existing node's depends_on.
- Titles and statements are copied verbatim from those nodes.

3. Assembly, following the selected proof.
(i) For each j, apply strip_distribution to μ_j, f, G, a, b, using continuity of f and μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}) < ∞. Choose F_j. It is monotone, satisfies ofReal(F_j(b) − F_j(a)) = μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}), and satisfies μ_j(G ∩ {t−h<f<t}) ≤ ofReal(F_j(t) − F_j(t−h)) for t ∈ (a,b) and h ∈ (0, t−a) (steps 2-3).

On it, ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j(G ∩ {t−h<f<t}) ≤ ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F_j(t) − F_j(t−h)). liminf_le_liminf and monotone multiplication by L turn the hypothesis on Z_j into the hypothesis of monotone_majorant: Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F_j(t) − F_j(t−h)) (step 3 into step 4).
(iii) monotone_majorant gives a measurable g with liminf_j Z_j ≤ g a.e. on (a,b) and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ L·liminf_j ofReal(F_j(b) − F_j(a)). By (i) this bound equals L·liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}) (steps 5-9).

subproblems.title: Monotone distribution function controlling the strip masses of an arbitrary set
subproblems.statement: Let μ be a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^P (for a non-measurable set E, μ(E) denotes the outer-measure value, as for Mathlib measures), f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, G ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary (possibly non-measurable) and a, b ∈ ℝ with μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞. Then there is a nondecreasing F : ℝ → ℝ such that ENNReal.ofReal(F(b) − F(a)) = μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}), and μ(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) for every t ∈ (a, b) and every h ∈ (0, t − a).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Set (Euclid P)) (a b : ℝ), Continuous f → μ (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}) < ∞ → ∃ F : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone F ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (F b - F a) = μ (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}) ∧ ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, ∀ h ∈ Ioo 0 (t - a), μ (G ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (F t - F (t - h))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 3 of the selected proof of `dmcbr_slice_mass_majorant` ("Distribution functions", "Slice estimate"), for a single measure μ; F below is exactly that proof's F_j when μ = μ_j. The selected proof had already assumed a < b in its step 1. This statement has no such hypothesis, so step 3 below adds the case b ≤ a of the endpoint identity explicitly. Notation: A(s) := G ∩ {x : a < f(x) < s} for s ∈ ℝ, and ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal. Measures take values in [0, ∞]. For an arbitrary (possibly non-measurable) set E, μ(E) is the outer-measure value, as for Mathlib measures, so μ is monotone on all sets.
Book provenance: this is the precise form of the monotonicity remark between 4.9 and 4.10 of Simon Ch. 6 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1367-1372: "M_W(T⌞{f < t}) is increasing in t ..."). It fills in one detail the book leaves implicit: G is an arbitrary, possibly non-measurable set, so the splitting is done only along the Borel strip.

1. Monotonicity and finiteness of A. If s ≤ s′ then A(s) ⊆ A(s′), because a < f(x) < s ≤ s′. If s ≤ a then A(s) = ∅, because a < f(x) < s ≤ a is impossible. If s ≤ b then A(s) ⊆ A(b) = G ∩ {a < f < b}, so μ(A(s)) ≤ μ(A(b)) < ∞ (measure_mono and the hypothesis).

2. Definition and monotonicity of F. Put F(s) := (μ(A(min(s, b)))).toReal ∈ [0, ∞). Since min(s, b) ≤ b, step 1 gives μ(A(min(s, b))) < ∞, hence ofReal(F(s)) = μ(A(min(s, b))) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). If s ≤ s′ then min(s, b) ≤ min(s′, b) (min_le_min_right). So μ(A(min(s, b))) ≤ μ(A(min(s′, b))) < ∞ by step 1, and F(s) ≤ F(s′) (ENNReal.toReal_mono). Thus F is monotone.

3. Endpoint identity ofReal(F(b) − F(a)) = μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}) = μ(A(b)).
(a) Case b ≤ a. Then A(b) = ∅ by step 1, so the right side is μ(∅) = 0. Also min(b, b) = b and min(a, b) = b, so F(b) − F(a) = 0 and the left side is ofReal 0 = 0.
(b) Case a < b. Then min(a, b) = a, so F(a) = (μ(A(a))).toReal = (μ(∅)).toReal = 0 by step 1. Also min(b, b) = b, so ofReal(F(b) − F(a)) = ofReal((μ(A(b))).toReal) = μ(A(b)) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, using μ(A(b)) < ∞).

4. Strip estimate. Let t ∈ (a, b) and h ∈ (0, t − a), and put s := t − h. Then a < s < t < b, so min(t, b) = t and min(s, b) = s. By step 2, ofReal(F(t)) = μ(A(t)) and ofReal(F(s)) = μ(A(s)), and both are finite.
Let S := {x : s < f(x) < t} = {x : s < f(x)} ∩ {x : f(x) < t}. Because f is continuous, S is open (isOpen_lt for each part), hence a Borel, i.e. measurable, set (IsOpen.measurableSet). Split the arbitrary set A(t) along the measurable set S (Carathéodory's criterion, measure_inter_add_sdiff): μ(A(t) ∩ S) + μ(A(t) ∖ S) = μ(A(t)).
(i) A(t) ∩ S = G ∩ S. The inclusion "⊆" is clear. Conversely, if x ∈ G and s < f(x) < t, then a < s < f(x) < t, so x ∈ A(t).
(ii) A(s) ⊆ A(t) ∖ S. If x ∈ G and a < f(x) < s, then f(x) < s < t, so x ∈ A(t). Moreover f(x) < s excludes s < f(x), so x ∉ S.
By (i), (ii) and monotonicity of μ: μ(G ∩ S) + μ(A(s)) ≤ μ(A(t) ∩ S) + μ(A(t) ∖ S) = μ(A(t)).
Since μ(A(s)) ≠ ∞, subtraction in [0, ∞] gives μ(G ∩ S) ≤ μ(A(t)) − μ(A(s)) (ENNReal.le_sub_of_add_le_right). Finally μ(A(t)) − μ(A(s)) = ofReal(F(t)) − ofReal(F(s)) = ofReal(F(t) − F(s)) (ENNReal.ofReal_sub, using F(s) ≥ 0). As s = t − h and G ∩ S = G ∩ {t − h < f < t}, this reads μ(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) ≤ ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)).

5. Conclusion. The function F of step 2 is monotone (step 2) and satisfies the endpoint identity (step 3) and the strip estimate (step 4). This proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: A(s) := G ∩ {a < f < s} increases with s, is ∅ for s ≤ a, and μ(A(s)) ≤ μ(A(b)) < ∞ for s ≤ b.
F(s) := μ(A(min(s, b))).toReal is monotone (ENNReal.toReal_mono), and ofReal(F(s)) = μ(A(min(s, b))).
Endpoint identity ofReal(F(b) − F(a)) = μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}). If b ≤ a, both sides are 0. If a < b, then F(a) = 0 and ENNReal.ofReal_toReal applies.

For t ∈ (a, b) and h ∈ (0, t − a), split the arbitrary set A(t) along the open, hence measurable, strip S = {t − h < f < t} (measure_inter_add_sdiff). This gives μ(G ∩ S) + μ(A(t − h)) ≤ μ(A(t)), hence μ(G ∩ S) ≤ ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)).

subproblems.title: Lebesgue's inequality ∫⁻ over (a, b) of F′ ≤ F(b) − F(a) for monotone F
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ → ℝ be nondecreasing and a, b ∈ ℝ. Then ∫⁻_{t ∈ (a, b)} ENNReal.ofReal(F′(t)) dt ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(F(b) − F(a)). Here F′(t) = deriv F t is the derivative where it exists and 0 otherwise, and ∫⁻ is the [0, ∞]-valued lower Lebesgue integral.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (F : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ), Monotone F → ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, ENNReal.ofReal (deriv F t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (F b - F a)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the selected proof of `dmcbr_slice_mass_majorant` ("Lebesgue's inequality for one monotone function"). That step proves exactly this claim through the Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure. It is the selected proof's replacement for MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc: Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.DerivIntegrable is outside the frozen import closure, and its two lemmas are unknown constants after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`. The selected proof applied the claim with a < b. Every step below holds for arbitrary a, b, so no case distinction is needed; if b ≤ a, then (a, b) = ∅ and the left side is 0 anyway. Conventions: deriv F t is the derivative of F at t where it exists and 0 otherwise. λ is Lebesgue measure, ∫⁻ is the [0, ∞]-valued Lebesgue integral, and ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal. Also leftLim R y := lim_{x↑y} R(x) and rightLim F x := lim_{y↓x} F(y).
Book provenance: Simon Ch. 6, the remark between 4.9 and 4.10 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1367-1372): t ↦ M_W(T⌞{f < t}) "is increasing in t, hence is differentiable for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ and ∫_a^b d/dt M_W(T⌞{f<t}) dt ≤ M_W(T⌞{a<f<b})". This is Lebesgue's inequality ∫_a^b F′ ≤ F(b) − F(a) for nondecreasing F.

1. Stieltjes function. Let R := hF.stieltjesFunction (Monotone.stieltjesFunction) be the Stieltjes function of the monotone F. As a function, R(x) = rightLim F x = F(x+) (Monotone.stieltjesFunction_eq). R is nondecreasing and right-continuous. Let ρ := R.measure be its Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure. For all x, y ∈ ℝ, ρ((x, y)) = ofReal(leftLim R y − R(x)) (StieltjesFunction.measure_Ioo, which has no hypotheses on x, y).

2. Lebesgue's differentiation theorem. For λ-a.e. t, F has derivative (ρ.rnDeriv λ t).toReal at t (Monotone.ae_hasDerivAt). At such t, deriv F t = (ρ.rnDeriv λ t).toReal (HasDerivAt.deriv). Hence ofReal(deriv F t) = ofReal((ρ.rnDeriv λ t).toReal) ≤ ρ.rnDeriv λ t (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le).

3. Comparison of integrals. The a.e. inequality of step 2 also holds a.e. for λ restricted to (a, b) (ae_restrict_of_ae). So by lintegral_mono_ae
∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F t) dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ρ.rnDeriv λ dλ.
Next, ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ρ.rnDeriv λ dλ ≤ (λ.withDensity(ρ.rnDeriv λ))((a, b)) (withDensity_apply_le, valid for every set). By the Lebesgue decomposition, λ.withDensity(ρ.rnDeriv λ) ≤ ρ (Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_le, evaluated at (a, b) via Measure.le_iff'). So the last quantity is at most ρ((a, b)), and ρ((a, b)) = ofReal(leftLim R b − R(a)) by step 1.

4. Comparison of R with F.
(i) F(a) ≤ rightLim F a = R(a) (Monotone.le_rightLim with a ≤ a).
(ii) For every y < b, R(y) = rightLim F y ≤ F(b) (Monotone.rightLim_le with y < b). Since R is monotone, R(y) → leftLim R b as y → b along 𝓝[<] b (Monotone.tendsto_leftLim). The inequality R(y) ≤ F(b) holds on (−∞, b), which belongs to 𝓝[<] b (self_mem_nhdsWithin), and 𝓝[<] b is a nontrivial filter on ℝ. Passing to the limit gives leftLim R b ≤ F(b) (le_of_tendsto).
Hence leftLim R b − R(a) ≤ F(b) − F(a). Since ofReal is monotone (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal), ofReal(leftLim R b − R(a)) ≤ ofReal(F(b) − F(a)).

5. Conclusion. Combining steps 3 and 4: ∫⁻_{t ∈ (a,b)} ofReal(deriv F t) dt ≤ ρ((a, b)) = ofReal(leftLim R b − R(a)) ≤ ofReal(F(b) − F(a)). ∎
proof_key_steps: R := hF.stieltjesFunction (R = F(·+)) has measure ρ, and ρ((a, b)) = ofReal(leftLim R b − R(a)) (StieltjesFunction.measure_Ioo).
By Lebesgue's theorem (Monotone.ae_hasDerivAt), deriv F = (dρ/dλ).toReal a.e., so ofReal(deriv F) ≤ dρ/dλ a.e. (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le).
∫⁻ over (a, b) of ofReal(deriv F) ≤ ∫⁻ over (a, b) of dρ/dλ ≤ λ.withDensity(dρ/dλ)((a, b)) ≤ ρ((a, b)) (lintegral_mono_ae, withDensity_apply_le, Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_le).
F(a) ≤ R(a) and leftLim R b ≤ F(b) (Monotone.le_rightLim, Monotone.rightLim_le, Monotone.tendsto_leftLim, le_of_tendsto). So ofReal(leftLim R b − R(a)) ≤ ofReal(F(b) − F(a)).

subproblems.title: Left difference quotients in [0, ∞] at a point of differentiability
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ → ℝ be differentiable at t ∈ ℝ. Then liminf_{h→0⁺} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹) · ENNReal.ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(F′(t)), with the liminf taken along the filter 𝓝[>] 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (F : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ), DifferentiableAt ℝ F t → liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * ENNReal.ofReal (F t - F (t - h))) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (deriv F t)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the selected proof of `dmcbr_slice_mass_majorant` ("Bound at differentiability points"). In that step the left difference quotients h⁻¹(F_j(t) − F_j(t − h)) converge to deriv F_j t as h ↓ 0 (HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_left after the substitution h ↦ −h). For h > 0 the product ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F_j(t) − F_j(t − h)) equals ofReal(h⁻¹(F_j(t) − F_j(t − h))) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). The liminf along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0 is then bounded by the limit. This child isolates that limit argument for a single function. The comparison of the strip masses with these quotients (step 3 of the selected proof) is carried out in the parent assembly. Monotonicity of F is not needed. Write D := F′(t) = deriv F t and ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal.
Book provenance: Simon Ch. 6, 4.9 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1356-1365) bounds the slice mass by ess sup_W|Df| · liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ M_W(T⌞{t − h < f < t}). Wherever the increasing function t ↦ M_W(T⌞{f < t}) is differentiable, this liminf is at most its derivative. The book uses this step at lines 1367-1372, and again in (2) of the proof of 8.2 (lines 2343-2347).

1. Since F is differentiable at t, F has derivative D at t (DifferentiableAt.hasDerivAt).

2. Left difference quotients. By HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_left, s⁻¹ · (F(t + s) − F(t)) → D as s → 0 along 𝓝[<] 0. The map h ↦ −h sends 𝓝[>] 0 into 𝓝[<] 0 (tendsto_neg_nhdsGT with a = 0, simplified by −0 = 0). Composing the two limits, (−h)⁻¹ · (F(t + (−h)) − F(t)) → D as h → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0. For every real h, (−h)⁻¹ · (F(t − h) − F(t)) = −h⁻¹ · (F(t − h) − F(t)) = h⁻¹ · (F(t) − F(t − h)) (inv_neg and ring arithmetic). Hence q(h) := h⁻¹ · (F(t) − F(t − h)) → D along 𝓝[>] 0.

3. Passing to [0, ∞]. Since ofReal is continuous, ofReal(q(h)) → ofReal(D) along 𝓝[>] 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal). For h > 0 we have h⁻¹ ≥ 0, so ofReal(q(h)) = ofReal(h⁻¹) · ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, which only needs the first factor to be nonnegative). The set (0, ∞) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). So φ(h) := ofReal(h⁻¹) · ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) agrees with ofReal(q(h)) eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, and therefore φ(h) → ofReal(D) along 𝓝[>] 0 (Tendsto.congr').

4. Conclusion. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial, and [0, ∞] is a complete linear order with the order topology. So the liminf of the convergent function φ equals its limit (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq): liminf_{h→0⁺} φ(h) = ofReal(D). In particular liminf_{h→0⁺} φ(h) ≤ ofReal(deriv F t). ∎
proof_key_steps: HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_left composed with h ↦ −h (tendsto_neg_nhdsGT) gives h⁻¹(F(t) − F(t − h)) → deriv F t along 𝓝[>] 0.
For h > 0, ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) = ofReal(h⁻¹(F(t) − F(t − h))) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). This tends to ofReal(deriv F t) (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal, Tendsto.congr').
On the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0 the liminf of a convergent function equals its limit (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq).

subproblems.title: Measurable Fatou majorant from left difference quotients of monotone functions
subproblems.statement: Let F_j : ℝ → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) be nondecreasing, Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞], a, b ∈ ℝ and L ∈ ℝ≥0. Suppose Z_j(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0⁺} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹) · ENNReal.ofReal(F_j(t) − F_j(t − h)) for all j and all t ∈ (a, b). Then there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] such that liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b), and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_j ENNReal.ofReal(F_j(b) − F_j(a)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (F : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (Z : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (a b : ℝ) (L : NNReal), (∀ j, Monotone (F j)) → (∀ (j : ℕ) (t : ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → Z j t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * ENNReal.ofReal (F j t - F j (t - h))) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → liminf (fun j => Z j t) atTop ≤ g t) ∧ ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun j => ENNReal.ofReal (F j b - F j a)) atTop
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4-7 and 9 of the selected proof of `dmcbr_slice_mass_majorant` ("Bound at differentiability points", "Exceptional null set", "Definition and measurability of g", "The a.e. bound", "Fatou"). The strip masses S_j(t, h) are replaced here by their upper bounds ofReal(F_j(t) − F_j(t − h)), and step 8 enters through a sibling. The proof uses two sibling results, each applied to every F_j:
- cbr_smm_liminf_left_slope_le_deriv (sibling left_slope): for every H : ℝ → ℝ differentiable at t, liminf_{h→0⁺} ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(H(t) − H(t − h)) ≤ ofReal(deriv H t).
- cbr_smm_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le (sibling lintegral_deriv): for every monotone H : ℝ → ℝ and all a, b ∈ ℝ, ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv H t) dt ≤ ofReal(H(b) − H(a)).
Values lie in [0, ∞], L is finite, and ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal. λ is Lebesgue measure, and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} integrates with respect to λ restricted to (a, b). No assumption a < b is needed.
Book provenance: the integrated form 4.10 of Simon Ch. 6 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1367-1377), stated for a sequence with liminf_j and Fatou's lemma. Remark 8.3(1) needs this form (lines 2311-2316: "for some subsequence {j′}").

1. Densities. For j ∈ ℕ put d_j(t) := ofReal(deriv F_j t). For every F_j the function deriv F_j : ℝ → ℝ is Borel measurable (measurable_deriv), so d_j is measurable (Measurable.ennreal_ofReal).

2. Definition and measurability of g. Put g(t) := L · liminf_{j→∞} d_j(t). The pointwise liminf of the measurable sequence (d_j) is measurable (Measurable.liminf). Multiplication by the constant L preserves measurability (Measurable.const_mul), so g is measurable.

3. Exceptional null set. Each F_j is monotone, hence differentiable at λ-a.e. t by Lebesgue's theorem (Monotone.ae_differentiableAt). Since ℕ is countable, for λ-a.e. t every F_j is differentiable at t (ae_all_iff).

4. The a.e. bound. Let t lie in the full-measure set of step 3 with t ∈ (a, b), and let j ∈ ℕ. The sibling left_slope, applied to F_j at t, gives liminf_{h→0⁺} ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F_j(t) − F_j(t − h)) ≤ d_j(t). Multiplication by L is monotone on [0, ∞]. With the hypothesis this gives Z_j(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0⁺} ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F_j(t) − F_j(t − h)) ≤ L · d_j(t) for every j. Therefore
liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ liminf_j (L · d_j(t)) = L · liminf_j d_j(t) = g(t).
The inequality is liminf_le_liminf, applied to a bound that holds for every j; its boundedness side conditions are automatic in the complete lattice [0, ∞]. The equality is ENNReal.liminf_const_mul_of_ne_top, using L ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.coe_ne_top) and that atTop on ℕ is nontrivial. This proves: for λ-a.e. t, t ∈ (a, b) implies liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t).

5. Integral bound.
(i) ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g = L · ∫⁻_{(a,b)} liminf_j d_j, by lintegral_const_mul and the measurability of liminf_j d_j from step 2.
(ii) ∫⁻_{(a,b)} liminf_j d_j ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻_{(a,b)} d_j, by Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le, for the measurable d_j of step 1 and the countably generated filter atTop). Multiplying by L preserves the inequality.
(iii) For each j, ∫⁻_{(a,b)} d_j ≤ ofReal(F_j(b) − F_j(a)), by the sibling lintegral_deriv applied to the monotone F_j. By liminf_le_liminf, liminf_j ∫⁻_{(a,b)} d_j ≤ liminf_j ofReal(F_j(b) − F_j(a)), and multiplying by L preserves the inequality.
Chaining (i)-(iii) gives ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ L · liminf_j ofReal(F_j(b) − F_j(a)).

6. Conclusion. By steps 2, 4 and 5, g is measurable, dominates liminf_j Z_j λ-a.e. on (a, b), and satisfies the integral bound. This proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: d_j := ofReal ∘ deriv F_j is measurable (measurable_deriv), and so is g := L · liminf_j d_j (Measurable.liminf, Measurable.const_mul).
For λ-a.e. t, every F_j is differentiable at t (Monotone.ae_differentiableAt, ae_all_iff).
At such t ∈ (a, b), the left_slope sibling gives Z_j(t) ≤ L·d_j(t). So liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_j d_j(t) = g(t) (liminf_le_liminf, ENNReal.liminf_const_mul_of_ne_top).
∫⁻ g = L·∫⁻ liminf_j d_j ≤ L·liminf_j ∫⁻ d_j ≤ L·liminf_j ofReal(F_j(b) − F_j(a)) (lintegral_const_mul, Fatou's lintegral_liminf_le, lintegral_deriv sibling).
